Step 4: Demonstrate the proof We will present and share with you case studies from previous installations similar to yours that demonstrate the benefits and energy saving results that can be achieved. Step 5: Installation and log results On your instruction we will install the correct equipment on your site for you. Our authorised service engineers will use the latest state of the art power analysers and software to record the actual energy used and contrast against our predicted results. Step 6: Confirmation of projected saving and claiming of available grant moneys In conclusion, we confirm in a final report your payback time, annual savings and reduction in energy used ready for your to claim Enhanced Capital Allowances, ECA and or grants available from the Sustainable Energy fund. The drive is equipped with built-in features that simplify ordering and delivery, and reduces commissioning costs, since everything is provided in a single, compact package. The drives share the same user interfaces and options, enabling users to use the knowledge gained with the ACS580 drives. Other built-in features include EMC filter, brake chopper up to frame R3, Modbus fieldbus interface and safe torque off (STO). The plug-in fieldbus adapter modules enable connectivity with all major automation systems. Control panel’s straightforward settings menu and embedded assistants reduce time needed for drive commissioning. The menus are clearly named by function, such as motor, ramp and limit settings. The free to download Drive composer PC tool offers extensive drive monitoring and process tuning capabilities. Drive’s energy optimizer control mode ensures the maximum torque per ampere, reducing energy drawn from the supply. The built-in energy calculators, including used and saved kWh, CO2 reduction and money saved, help the user monitor and fine-tune processes to ensure optimal energy use. pages.text: ABB Power Quality ABB PQF active filters are the ultimate answer to tough Power Quality problems caused by harmonics, load unbalance and reactive power demand. Advantage Control can apply ABB PQF active filters to small, medium or large applications and are suitable for both industrial and commercial installations in LV networks. They can also be employed in MV networks through the use of a coupling transformer. Poor power quality can  cause : reduced energy efficiency due to harmonics in the network overheating of cables, switchgear, motors and transformers damage to sensitive electronic equipment tripping of circuit breakers and blowing fuses premature ageing of the installation capacitor overloading and failures high current in neutral conductors excitation of network resonance penalties from the utility company if harmonic levels are too high. The ABB PQF Range provides innovative solutions to actively clean the supply from harmonics, to produce smooth reactive power compensation and carry out load balancing. This feature is useful on a 4-wire system in particular as it allows for the much needed reduction of neutral to earth voltages. The PQF is not susceptible to large network impedance changes due to for example, paralleling of sources, or switching the mains supply to a generator power source.  It monitors the line current continuously processing the measured harmonics as digital signals utilising a high power processor) based system. The PQF also offers communication facilities.  Depending on your communication network, different solutions are available ranging from several digital I/O contacts to an optional Modbus RTU communication interface. Read more about how Power Quality Filters work. Call us today on 02844 613 782 and see how our Power Quality Filter can improve Power Quality in your business. Download PQF Pamphlet Product Details ABB active filters Have unprecedented filtering efficiency thanks to the unique closed loop control system and individual harmonic selection capability. Can perform stepless reactive power compensation of both inductive and capacitive loads. Can perform load balancing in both 3- and 4-wire systems. Raise system reliability to unprecedented levels thanks to full redundancy functionality. Are designed with the end customer in mind. pages.title: Encapsulated Motors - Advantage Control
pages.text: Encapsulated Motors A complete solution against the ingress of moisture. A simple solution from Advantage Control Ltd, that allows you to operate motors and VSD’s in areas with high levels of moisture or protection from washdown processes. One of the main reasons, especially for motor failures, has always been the ingress of water. A perfect solution is now available from Advantage Control that virtually eliminates the effects of water on a motor by completely encapsulating the winding and terminal box in an epoxy resin. The resin coated stator winding and resin filled terminal box are a safe solution to the presence of very high levels of moisture; as found in food processing, water treatment, car/pressure washer systems etc. ULTIMATE Solution In certain applications the ideal combination, for complete sealing and mechanical integrity, is the removal of the terminal box and gland.  The winding ends are crimped to a cable of specified length and then submerged in resin.  A steel plate is attached to complete the mechanical protection. This cable can then be attached directly into an ABB IP66 Variable Speed Drive; offering the ultimate solution for energy saving and water ingress.  As an added benefit, the motor runs cooler due to the improved thermal transfer. pages.title: DriveCare | Prevent Downtime | Advantage Control
pages.text: DriveCare Avoid any downtime in your production process. The Challenge To protect your plant and process from the unknown. As a Variable Speed Drive user some of your equipment is dependent on the efficient running of your Drives. But what if there were a problem, would you be covered? What would happen if one of my Variable Speed Drives f ailed? A Drive failure could result in a production failure, it can be that simple. But the question is, what would you do about it? Sure you could get a quick replacement using our DriveUpGrade service, but would you have all of the correct settings and parameters ready and waiting to get the Drive up and running? W h at details would I need if I replaced a Variable Speed Drive ? Every plant and process are different. Some Drives need more information than others to allow them to operate at optimum efficiency, but all Drives need data. There are a multitude of software parameters, serial numbers and plant/process descriptions required. How long would it take to find and input these details? Put simply, how long is a piece of string? It’s dependent on the individual application, but one thing’s for certain, if you don’t have them readily available, downtime will be extended in the event of a problem. W h ere would they be kept? When your Drives were initially commissioned, all of these details should have been documented for future use. All Drive updates should have been logged when plant/process changes were made. These key documents are often kept with the Drive itself or within large maintenance files. W h at if we don’t have the Drive settings or they are out of date? If the Drive parameters are misplaced or out of date, when the time comes for a replacement, you could be left with some expensive downtime. Our team can re-program your products and have your process running perfectly – but it can take considerably longer to do so. I know where the details for my Drives are, but I’m not sure what to do with them Having all your Drive’s details in one place is best practice, and will save valuable time in the event of an emergency, but is there anybody onsite that will know how to re-program a new product quickly and efficiently? The Solution Simple; DriveCare. It’s a bit like a dynamic insurance plan for the data controlling your AC Variable Speed Drives, designed to prevent downtime of each and every one within your plant or process. W e’ve got you covered Downtime is one of the largest threats to any production process. DriveCare gives you total peace of mind.  The service provides backup of all essential data. P lanned Maintenance We offer a range of services whereby we visit your plant periodically and thoroughly inspect your AC Drive products. Not only do DriveCare users qualify for preferential rates, but the chances of unexpected Drive failure are considerably reduced thanks to a careful monitoring system. P lant Catalogue All Drives and Motors can be logged into a complete plant-wide catalog, providing immediate access to the data settings for those products that need to be maintained, UpGraded or replaced. Call us today To find out more about how our DriveCare program could be helping you and your business, contact us today so that you’re covered for tomorrow. Service Details During commissioning, a backup is made of all software parameters, serial numbers and plant descriptions, which is then stored remotely on our own secure servers. There’s no need to go trawling through maintenance files or other documentation at those critical moments, when time is of the essence. We can even take ‘off-the-shelf Drives’ and restore all the software parameters before replacing it on your site, keeping any possible downtime to the absolute minimum. pages.title: Why Drives Can Fail - Advantage Control
pages.text: Why Drives Can Fail A drive, any drive, could theoretically last for a lifetime, but only if properly taken care of. Modern variable-speed drives (VSDs) are exceptionally reliable these days, but they’re not indestructible. That said, if you notice similar persistent or repeated trips in a VSD, then chances are that the drive isn’t actually the problem. If such trips are ignored (eg overtemperature), they can sometimes result in the failure of the drive. This video has been created by APDS Ltd, ABB AVPs for the South West in Bristol, to explain why drives can fail. Incorrect installation This is the single most important contributory factor to drives tripping or failing, and yet the one that should in theory be the easiest to avoid. For starters, the ambient temperature around the drive shouldn’t exceed 40 °C. If the location of the drive makes this impossible then there are ways around it, for instance by cooling the drive externally, but this isn’t an ideal solution and will of course increase energy usage. It’s also important to keep the drive dust-free, as dust can impede the air-flow and lead to overheating. The drive must be kept dry, as moisture will corrode the circuit boards over time. This can be difficult in, for instance, the food industry where equipment has to be regularly washed down, but again there are ways around it such as mounting the drive in an enclosure with the appropriate ingress protection (IP) rating. Any ABB authorised value provider will know all of this, but it’s up to you,the customer,  to ensure that the AVP is briefed properly on exactly where and how the drive will be used. Poor maintenance Planned maintenance is far more cost-effective than unplanned breakdown repair, so to prolong the life of your drive as well as saving time and money, it is vital to have in place a programme of preventive maintenance. ABB and its authorised value providers offer a range of maintenance services to suit your needs, from annual inspections all the way up to remote monitoring services that can tell ABB that something’s amiss in your drive long before it displays any signs of wear. Whilst these things are generally best left to the pros, there are some maintenance activities you can carry out yourself. Spraying compressed air (make sure it’s dry and oil-free) through the heat sink fan will help to keep it clear of dust, and checking connections can prevent arcing from heat cycles and mechanical vibrations. The capacitors in a drive will also wear out over time (usually 5-10 years) and require replacing, so this is something that needs to be checked. Capacitors work much like batteries, and so if the drive is rarely run at full output it’s a good idea to power it up every six months or so to ensure that the capacitors remain at peak performance capability. Excessive loads When an operator gets to know their machine it’s natural to want to push the boundaries and see what it can do. Your drive won’t thank you for running it over its rated level. Often drives are run over capacity due to a lack of experience and/or training, so it’s important to ensure that all operators are aware that running a drive beyond its capabilities can and will damage it. For help and advice maintaining your ABB drive population, please contact us. pages.text: Advantage Control ActiFlow system and ABB HVAC Inverter Drives improve retail store environment and saves energy Energy savings of 30% were achieved. The Problem At the company’s newest, 29,000 square metre retail store in N Ireland, the AHU, hot water and biomass boiler control panels operated the pumps by DOL start with control of flow by throttle valve. This method of control left little room for flexibility and was wasteful of energy. Advantage Control’s Solution Thanks to Advantage Control’s ActivFlow system and ABB HVAC ASH550 variable speed drives (VSD), the store environment has been improved and an energy saving of 30% has been achieved. The Full Story At the company’s newest 29,000 square metre store in N Ireland, the AHU, hot water and biomass boiler electrical control panels operated the pumps on DOL start with control of flow by throttle valve. This method of control left little room for flexibility with control options limited to either on /off, or throttled and is wasteful of energy. An energy appraisal was conducted by Advantage Control. Using a state of the art energy meter, to identify actual energy consumed. Using ABB’s dedicated fan and pump energy saving software, the findings were analysed and potential savings recorded. Following analysis of the data and presentation of the results, six ABB ACH550 HVAC inverter drives (VSDs) with ActiFlow were installed. As a result, flow rates were matched automatically to the stores environmental requirements at any given time leading to a more comfortable experience for both staff and customers. In addition, using ABBs HVAC ACH550 variable speed drives (VSD) with ActiFlow system, energy savings of 30% were achieved. pages.text: Advantage Control ActiFlow system and ABB’s Dedicated water industry ACQ810 Inverter Drive improve water utilities process and reduces callouts Advantage Control provides solution to eradicate water pumping station's issues. The Problem At a remote unmanned water pumping station, the high lift pumps operated by Soft-Starts delivered high pressure in the pipe work on start-up and caused the dossing pumps to be knocked out. This affected water quality which incurred financial penalty and in addition, required site attendance by an engineer to reset the dosing pumps. Advantage Control’s Solution Thanks to Advantage Control’s ActivFlow system and ABB’s ACQ810 dedicated water industry variable speed drive (VSD), the problems at the station have been eradicated. The Full Story At a remote unmanned water pumping station, the high lift pumps operated by Soft-Starts delivered high pressure in the pipe work on start-up and caused the dossing pumps to be knocked out. This affected water quality which incurred financial penalty and in addition, required site attendance by an engineer to reset the dosing pumps. Data logging was conducted by Advantage Control to monitor the load pattern under Soft –Start control using a state of the art data logger to identify the actual energy consumed and periods of pump operation. The results were analysed and potential improvements noted. Following analysis of the data and presentation of the results, a decision was taken to remove the Soft-Start and because of the ACQ810’s low volume to power ratio, it was possible to install the ABB ACQ810 inverter drives (VSD) with ActiFlow within the existing Soft –Start panel. As a result, the pressure generated within the pipe work on start-up was reduced, the dossing pump “Knock-out” eradicated and the site call outs reduced from 10 per month to 0. “This installation has been a great success and we are continuing to work with Advantage Control on other projects”. ~Site Manager Industries Automotive Electric Motor Rewinds Food & Beverage HVAC Market Laundries (Industrial) Manufacturing Plastic Extrusion Quarries Retail Water Utilities

pages.text: Advantage Control Drive Upgrade & regenerative Inverter Drive & motor improves control process and saves money. Our drive upgrade system and variable speed drives deliver excellent results. The Problem A world leading automotive manufacturer approached Advantage Control to improve production on one of their body shop press lines. Traditionally the presses were driven by an 110kW open frame electric motor with starting method by soft- start. This method of operation does not allow for process control during production. Advantage Control’s Solution Thanks to Advantage Control’s Drive Upgrade system and ABBs ACS800-17 IP54 cabinet variable speed drives (VSD), the manufacturing process has been improved and material wastage reduced saving ££££££££ per year. The Full Story A world leading automotive manufacture approached Advantage Control to improve production on one of their blanking press lines. Traditionally the presses are driven by a 110kW open frame IP23 electric motors operated by soft start. This method of operation does not allow for process control during production resulting in significant wastage of material as the process required speed matching for each specific pressed part. An application appraisal was conducted by Advantage Control Engineers in conjunction with the site Engineers. Using a state of the art energy meter, the operational duty cycle was analysed and potential process improvements were recorded. Following analysis of the data and presentation of the results, as part of a £4 million pound project, Advantage Control was awarded the turnkey project to upgrade the press. This entailed installing and commissioning the drive, motor, supply and control cabling and control architecture, integrating with the new robotic feeder line. An ABB Variable Speed drive (VSD) ACS800 IP54 regenerative cabinet drive and an ABB IP55 IE3 Process Performance motor, supply cable and Profibus control was supplied and installed. As a result, the press stroke is matched automatically to the robotically controlled feeder line speed significantly reducing the material wastage and saving money. pages.title: Advantage Control Help Window Company Make Clear Savings - Advantage Control
pages.text: Advantage Control Help Window Company Make Clear Savings We implement solution to reduce energy costs by over 40%! The Problem A window manufacturer making frames for projects across the United Kingdom contacted Advantage Control to carry out an energy survey on their processes to help them reduce energy costs and save money. Advantage Control’s Solution After carrying out the survey we were able to make recommendations and implement solutions to help reduce energy costs. In total the energy saved on a weekly basis for the main extraction was in excess of 40% for the main extraction system! Advantage Control provided logging on the customers’ plant before and after to demonstrate the results. They also set-up a hire drive to demonstrate the potential for energy saving. The Full Story A window manufacturer making frames for projects across the United Kingdom contacted Advantage Control to carry out an energy survey on their processes. Being in a rural location meant that finding a balance on the power used was crucial to plans for expansion and in problems associated with power usage on a limited supply. After energy appraisal carried out by trained engineers the key areas using fans where identified for energy saving. These where – Oven Convection Fans Spray Extraction Fans Main Extraction Fans The oven convection fans had been causing problems with air flow being too high and disturbing the finish of the painted product. An ABB ACS550 variable speed drive was fitted to each of the four motors providing complete control of the fan speed. After adjustment the fans were set to run at just 37Hz. The spray fans extract paint overspray to atmosphere. The speed of these is important as too much air flow causes more of the paint or lacquer to end up on the filters than the product. This has the opposite effect when the airflow is too low. Fine Tuning by the Clients engineers who were trained on site at the time of commissioning allows the operator to deliver the optimum paint to the product and achieve the best results. The extraction system is configured with different fans providing extraction to individual machines all controlled from a single cabinet. Five ABB IP54 drives fitted beside the cabinet allow the fan speed to be set. The optimal speed of a fan is often lower than the motors plated speed. By adjusting the frequency the fan is set to run at the minimum speed before a noticeable change in air velocity occurs. This offers a significant financial return in energy savings. The harmony of the solution was further improved by the installation of remote start and stop controls beside the operators existing control station. In total the energy saved on a weekly basis for the main extraction was in excess of 40% for the main extraction system! Advantage Control provided logging on the customers’ plant before and after to demonstrate the results. They also set-up a hire drive to demonstrate the potential for energy saving. “We instructed the Advantage Control team to carry out an energy appraisal on selected applications throughout the factory and come up with a solution to minimise our energy usage. A solution was found and after a trial period it was clear to see that huge savings could be made without any deterioration in quality of finished product. Advantage Control gave us excellent technical and financial guidance throughout the whole project – we would have no hesitation is using the Advantage Control team for future projects.” Industries Automotive Electric Motor Rewinds Food & Beverage HVAC Market Laundries (Industrial) Manufacturing Plastic Extrusion Quarries Retail Water Utilities

The Problem A leader in the manufacture of High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) bottles for the food and drink industry wanted to reduce its Carbon footprint and save costs. Having many Process Pumps – typical rating of 11-30KW,circulating water from the Chiller Units around the factory cooling manufacturing machines then back to the Chiller. If one pump cannot cope and the water is returning too hot, it is therefore necessary to bring in another pump and potentially wasting energy. Following a successful trial it was discovered that there were major savings available using ABB inverter control on the Chiller pumps on site. This manufacturer proceeded with confidence to save over 60% following optimisation on over 20 Chiller pumps at a number of their sites. Advantage Control’s Solution The existing Process and chiller pumps on site are currently controlled by Direct On Line starters, fixed speed with flow regulated by valve. This method of control uses more energy than necessary to achieve the required flow and is an ideal application for innovation and energy saving. Potential savings are very good with quick payback times possible. The Full Story An energy appraisal was undertaken on the Process and chiller pumps which showed potential saving and prompt payback time. We installed a trial unit so that the local site manager could witness the savings for himself. The Process and chiller pump’s energy consumption was monitored before and after. The ABB ACH550 used has many energy saving features, speed control and up to 25% lower harmonics with its integral Swinging choke. This ensures a low harmonic foot print as the choke is automatically tuned to the load conditions and that only the power needed for the process is delivered to the motor, running the pumps cooler and quieter. The savings recorded was 49% energy saving when compared with traditional DOL starting method. This was improved on final installations and the average savings made was 60% with average paybacks of 9-10months. Following analysis of the data and presentation of the results, 20 ABB ACH550 HVAC inverter drives (VSDs) with ActivFlow control were installed and valve control removed from the process. As a result, flow rates were matched automatically to the factory process requirements at any given time. By using this control method, the system will respond to any changes within the manufacturing process and keep the system at a constant temperature ensuring consistent product quality. pages.title: PrimePac Limited - Advantage Control
pages.text: PrimePac Limited SynRM investment leads to 30 percent increase in bottle production. Customer Benefits – Energy Saving: Up to 60 percent fall in energy costs on blow molding machine – CO2 Saving : Up to 80 tonnes of carbon dioxide saved – Higher Throughout : 30 percent more usable plastic bottles – Improved quality and consistency of bottles : DTC’s accurate speed regulation leads to consistent   length and weight of plastic through extruder – Less Waste : Speed regulation prevents erratic machine movements avoiding loss of plastic through varying tail lengths – Avoid High Replacement Cost: Saved $44,000 cost of refurbishing pump and drive with same technology – Fast Payback : $11,000 investment recovered within 12 months – Avoid upgrade of electrical capacity : Saved $356,000 cost upgrading from 600kVA to 800 kVA electrical supply which enables additional all-electric blow molding machine to be installed SynRM runs quieter than standard AC motor. A worn out hydraulic motor on a 23 year old blow molding machine at Northern Ireland’s PrimePac was using excessive energy and producing inaccurate speed holding, leading to poor quality plastic bottles. Container maker sees 60 percent fall in energy costs and 30 percent higher output. “Previously I could create a bottle in 10 seconds, delivering 50 grams of material,” explains Clifford Craig, Engineering Manager at PrimePac. “However, in recent years we had to run that bottle at 12 seconds because the extruder output wasn’t quick enough. The extruder had started to create long tails, which are basically excess plastic that needs to be trimmed and recycled.” Energy appraisal reveals machine failings. An energy appraisal carried out by Advantage Control, revealed a potential energy saving of up to 30 percent by replacing the hydraulic motor with a synchronous reluctance motor (SynRM) and drive package. The energy appraisal showed that the power use was erratic and consumption was high due to the hydraulic pack requiring extra torque on start up. “We came in and logged for one week, the energy use of the old machine against one of the existing all-electric models, both of which were making similar bottles of the same size and weight,” says David Watt, Technical Sales Adviser at Advantage Control Limited. “Our energy appraisal was carried out on the main incoming supply which guaranteed that we weren’t just seeing one particular motor. We looked at the entire machine and the efficiency across it. When we compared the efficiencies we could see that the old machine was consuming significantly more energy to carry out the same process.” However, once the SynRM package was installed the actual energy saving peaked at 60 percent. As a result, the $11,000 purchase of the 55 kW, IE4 SynRM package is expected to payback in under 12 months. Approximately 5% of the energy saving came from reducing the load on the 18.5 kW granulator that is used to chip waste plastic – long tails – cut from a bottle, before it is re-heated and fed back into the blow molder. The granulator and accompanying heating routine is energy intensive and the process was now using more electricity, as Craig explains: “This all takes extra energy which in effect is for making the same bottle that you made five minutes earlier. You take energy to make it, energy to convey it, energy to grind it, energy to drive the screw.” DTC improves speed regulation The savings on the granulator is a result of improved speed holding accuracy such that bottles of a uniform length and weight are now being produced. The highly accurate speed holding is a result of the encoderless feedback offered by the direct torque control technology of the ABB industrial drive. Whereas previously 63 percent of extrusions successfully turned into bottles, today this has increased to 96 percent. “The missing 4 percent is purely as the machine is ramping down,” says Watt. “So it has greatly improved the productivity as over 30 percent more bottles are fit for purpose.” Unexpected benefit Such are the energy savings that PrimePac was able to avoid a £250,000 ($356,000) upgrade of its 600 kVA electrical supply, needed to power an additional all-electric blow molding machine for producing a new type of medicine bottle. “We have 600 kVA of electricity coming into the company. We couldn’t install a new machine because we didn’t have the electric power; we were already peaking,” says Craig. “But with the 60 percent energy saving we achieved on the old blow molder we have been able to install another new all-electric blow molding machine. And even that machine is still not using all the 60 percent of energy we saved. This is beyond our wildest ambitions. We have managed to massively increase our production, just by installing one SynRM package from ABB.” Improved working conditions Other benefits of the installation include an improvement in the quality of the environment. “Now the operators can hear what their colleagues are saying while standing alongside the motor,” says Watt. “There are machines in the factory that are using standard AC motor technology and the SynRM package is running quieter than these comparable motors. Running cooler and quieter than the equivalent IE3 motor is an immediate demonstration of how much more efficient this motor is.” PrimePac Limited PrimePac Limited is located north west of Belfast in Northern Ireland. It specializes in continuous extrusion blow molding to manufacture a range of plastic bottles, containers and jars together with closures, pumps, sprays and various accessories. PrimePac invests extensively in new machinery, its staff and environmental initiatives. The company uses Advantage Control to help reduce its energy bills and lower maintenance costs through timely advice on speed control of its machinery.
